benchmarks.name: Long-form virology task 1 (Anthropic RSP)
benchmarks.description: Anthropic Responsible Scaling Policy CBRN/bio evaluation; scores are reported in the system cards only, with capability thresholds rather than a public leaderboard. End-to-end score reported 0-1 in the cards, written here 0-100; Anthropic treats above 80 as a notable-capability result.

benchmarks.name: Long-form virology task 2 (Anthropic RSP)
benchmarks.description: Anthropic Responsible Scaling Policy CBRN/bio evaluation; scores are reported in the system cards only, with capability thresholds rather than a public leaderboard. Second task in the same pair; end-to-end score written 0-100. Metric definition changed across cards (max-of-5, pass@5, mean).

benchmarks.name: DNA synthesis screening evaluation (count of targets cleared)
benchmarks.description: Anthropic Responsible Scaling Policy CBRN/bio evaluation; scores are reported in the system cards only, with capability thresholds rather than a public leaderboard. SecureBio-designed evaluation of biosecurity screening robustness. Recorded here as the number of the 10 evaluated targets on which the model met all grading criteria (0-10, not a percentage). Anthropic states the grader is a weak proxy and plans to deprecate the evaluation.

benchmarks.name: Biological-risk acquisition uplift trial (multiplier)
benchmarks.description: Anthropic Responsible Scaling Policy CBRN/bio evaluation; scores are reported in the system cards only, with capability thresholds rather than a public leaderboard. Human uplift trial: ratio of the model-assisted group score to the internet-only control group score (a multiplier, not a percentage). Anthropic pre-registered ~5x as a risk threshold and ~2.8x as acceptable.

benchmarks.name: Virology protocol uplift trial (multiplier)
benchmarks.description: Anthropic Responsible Scaling Policy CBRN/bio evaluation; scores are reported in the system cards only, with capability thresholds rather than a public leaderboard. Uplift multiplier in raw protocol score for model-assisted participants versus an internet-only control group (not a percentage).

benchmarks.name: Virology protocol uplift trial: mean critical failures
benchmarks.description: Anthropic Responsible Scaling Policy CBRN/bio evaluation; scores are reported in the system cards only, with capability thresholds rather than a public leaderboard. Mean number of critical-failure gates (out of 18) present in protocols written by model-assisted participants. LOWER is better; Anthropic rules out the capability below ~1.8.

benchmarks.name: Biology knowledge questions vs expert baseline (count)
benchmarks.description: Anthropic Responsible Scaling Policy CBRN/bio evaluation; scores are reported in the system cards only, with capability thresholds rather than a public leaderboard. Number of the 33 expert-written questions (graded by external domain experts) on which the model answered better than the human expert baseline. Anthropic set the threshold of concern at 27/33; scoring reliability is low because grading is manual.

benchmarks.name: Creative biology (SecureBio)
benchmarks.description: Anthropic Responsible Scaling Policy CBRN/bio evaluation; scores are reported in the system cards only, with capability thresholds rather than a public leaderboard. SecureBio question set probing unusual biology knowledge, used as a weak proxy. Mean score reported 0-1 in the cards, written here 0-100; SecureBio expects human experts around 10-14%.

benchmarks.name: Short-horizon computational biology tasks (tasks above rule-out bar)
benchmarks.description: Anthropic Responsible Scaling Policy CBRN/bio evaluation; scores are reported in the system cards only, with capability thresholds rather than a public leaderboard. Faculty.ai-built computational-biology/bioinformatics task suite. Recorded as the number of the 6 tasks on which the model crossed the lower-bound rule-out threshold (0-6).

benchmarks.name: Dyno black-box RNA task: prediction score
benchmarks.description: Anthropic Responsible Scaling Policy CBRN/bio evaluation; scores are reported in the system cards only, with capability thresholds rather than a public leaderboard. Dyno Therapeutics sequence-modelling challenge, benchmarked against 57 human ML-bio participants. Value is the Spearman correlation over all sequences (0-1).

benchmarks.name: Dyno black-box RNA task: design score (top sequence)
benchmarks.description: Anthropic Responsible Scaling Policy CBRN/bio evaluation; scores are reported in the system cards only, with capability thresholds rather than a public leaderboard. Design score of the best sequence proposed in the Dyno challenge (arbitrary functional units, not a percentage).

benchmarks.name: AAV capsid packaging prediction (AUROC)
benchmarks.description: Anthropic Responsible Scaling Policy CBRN/bio evaluation; scores are reported in the system cards only, with capability thresholds rather than a public leaderboard. Dyno gene-therapy capsid-assembly prediction task. AUROC (0-1) in the reasoning-only condition unless the entry says otherwise; the naive ESM-2 baseline is ~0.70.

benchmarks.name: BioMysteryBench (human-difficult subset)
benchmarks.description: Anthropic internal life-sciences capability evaluation (beneficial-use portfolio), reported in the Claude system cards. Subset that human experts did not solve but that has an objective ground-truth answer.

benchmarks.name: LatchBio SingleCellBench
benchmarks.description: Anthropic internal life-sciences capability evaluation (beneficial-use portfolio), reported in the Claude system cards. LatchBio evaluation of single-cell RNA-seq analysis workflows (195 problems).

benchmarks.name: BioPipelineBench Verified
benchmarks.description: Anthropic internal life-sciences capability evaluation (beneficial-use portfolio), reported in the Claude system cards. Execution of bioinformatics workflows (sequence analysis, assembly, chromatin profiling); validated problem subset.

benchmarks.name: Bioinformatics preprocessing evaluation (Anthropic)
benchmarks.description: Anthropic internal life-sciences capability evaluation (beneficial-use portfolio), reported in the Claude system cards. Basic sequencing-data preprocessing and analysis workflows extracted from published papers; human PhD baseline 62.3 on the baselined subset.

benchmarks.name: ProteinGym Hard
benchmarks.description: Anthropic internal life-sciences capability evaluation (beneficial-use portfolio), reported in the Claude system cards. Ranking mutant protein sequences against the wild type, scored by rank correlation with published ProteinGym lab measurements.

benchmarks.name: Protein design (sequence generation)
benchmarks.description: Anthropic internal life-sciences capability evaluation (beneficial-use portfolio), reported in the Claude system cards. benchmarks.name: Protein design library ranking

Prioritising designs from real protein-engineering campaigns; chance-normalised average precision (0 = random). The 83-problem set supersedes earlier versions.

benchmarks.name: De novo protein binder design campaign
benchmarks.description: Anthropic internal life-sciences capability evaluation (beneficial-use portfolio), reported in the Claude system cards. 24-hour autonomous design campaign per target (15 targets); submitted miniprotein binders are re-folded by a panel of structure predictors and scored on interface confidence, pose agreement and diversity.

benchmarks.name: Structural biology (open-ended)
benchmarks.description: Anthropic internal life-sciences capability evaluation (beneficial-use portfolio), reported in the Claude system cards. Open-ended questions relating biomolecular structure to function.

benchmarks.name: Phylogenetics

benchmarks.name: Lab protocols: troubleshooting
benchmarks.description: Anthropic internal life-sciences capability evaluation (beneficial-use portfolio), reported in the Claude system cards. Detecting and fixing errors in molecular-biology protocols, with web search available. Network access was removed from the task environment for the Opus 5.5 card re-runs.

benchmarks.name: Lab protocols: understanding
benchmarks.description: Anthropic internal life-sciences capability evaluation (beneficial-use portfolio), reported in the Claude system cards. Benchling-built evaluation of reading a published protocol and extending or adapting it. The Opus 5.5 card introduces a new held-out V2 set that is not comparable.

benchmarks.name: Morphology-to-molecule matching (Axiom Bio)

benchmarks.description: Successor to LAB-Bench: real-world biology research tasks (macro-average over 11 sub-tasks such as LitQA3, ProtocolQA2, FigQA2, DbQA2), typically run agentically with tools.

benchmarks.name: Multimodal Troubleshooting Virology (OpenAI Preparedness)
benchmarks.description: OpenAI Preparedness bio eval: 350 (later 322) SecureBio virology wet-lab troubleshooting questions, some with images. System cards up to o3/GPT-4.5 used a single-select variant (cons@32); GPT-5 onward use SecureBio's stricter multi-select scoring (pass@1), so values drop at the switch. Expert median ~22%.

benchmarks.name: ProtocolQA Open-Ended (OpenAI Preparedness)
benchmarks.description: 108 FutureHouse ProtocolQA multiple-choice questions rewritten by OpenAI as open-ended short answers: find and fix errors in published lab protocols. PhD expert baseline about 54%.

benchmarks.name: Tacit Knowledge and Troubleshooting (OpenAI Preparedness)
benchmarks.description: Unpublished 60-question multiple-choice set built with Gryphon Scientific covering tacit-knowledge and hands-on troubleshooting bottlenecks across the biothreat pipeline (cons@32). Consensus expert baseline 80%. Later cards also report a refusal-adjusted score.

benchmarks.name: TroubleshootingBench (OpenAI Preparedness)
benchmarks.description: 156 short-answer questions on 52 non-public, expert-written wet-lab protocols with realistic execution errors that rely on tacit hands-on knowledge (pass@1). 80th-percentile PhD expert baseline 36.4%.

scalingVectors.name: RL-trained test-time reasoning
scalingVectors.summary: OpenAI trained o1 with large-scale reinforcement learning to reason in a long private chain of thought, and showed that performance keeps improving with both train-time RL compute and test-time thinking time. That opened a second scaling axis beyond pretraining.

scalingVectors.name: Open recipe for RL on verifiable rewards
scalingVectors.summary: DeepSeek released R1's weights together with a full recipe: GRPO reinforcement learning with rule-based rewards on the V3 base, where R1-Zero developed long reasoning from pure RL with no supervised warm-up. o1-style reasoning became reproducible across the field.

scalingVectors.name: Hybrid reasoning with a user-set thinking budget
scalingVectors.summary: Anthropic billed Claude 3.7 Sonnet as the first hybrid reasoning model: one model that either answers at once or thinks at length. API users can cap its thinking at any token budget up to 128K, so test-time compute became a dial the user controls.

scalingVectors.name: Limits of pure pretraining scale
scalingVectors.summary: GPT-4.5 was OpenAI's largest pretraining run (about 3.8e26 FLOP by Epoch's estimate), yet its gains were modest for the cost. OpenAI called it its last non-chain-of-thought model and pulled it from the API in July 2025. GPT-5 then used less pretraining compute, which moved the frontier toward RL and inference-time scaling.

scalingVectors.name: Long-horizon agentic coding
scalingVectors.summary: Claude Opus 4 shipped alongside the general release of Claude Code. It could work continuously for several hours across thousands of steps; Rakuten ran a 7-hour autonomous open-source refactor with it. The length of task a model can finish became a scaling target.

scalingVectors.name: RL compute at pretraining scale
scalingVectors.summary: xAI ran reinforcement learning "at pretraining scale" on its 200,000-GPU Colossus cluster, using over an order of magnitude more RL compute than before on the Grok 3 base. Its launch chart showed RL compute roughly equal to pretraining compute.

scalingVectors.name: Parallel test-time compute
scalingVectors.summary: Grok 4 Heavy runs several agents in parallel that weigh multiple hypotheses before answering. It was the first publicly available product officially described as using parallel test-time compute. Gemini 2.5 Deep Think (previewed May 2025, released Aug 1) and GPT-5 Pro (Aug 7) followed. o1 pro mode (Dec 2024) was only reported to use parallel sampling.

scalingVectors.name: Agent-swarm orchestration trained with RL
scalingVectors.summary: Kimi K2.5 was trained with Parallel-Agent RL (PARL) to act as an orchestrator. It splits a task and directs a swarm of up to 100 sub-agents across up to 1,500 coordinated steps, with staged rewards so that it does not fall back to working alone. Moonshot reports up to 4.5x lower latency than a single agent.

scalingVectors.name: A model that helped build itself
scalingVectors.summary: OpenAI called GPT-5.3-Codex "our first model that was instrumental in creating itself". Early versions debugged its own training, managed its deployment and diagnosed evaluation results, an early sign of recursive self-improvement. GPT-5.6 Sol later ran the post-training of the smaller GPT-5.6 Luna.

scalingVectors.name: A frontier tier above Opus
scalingVectors.summary: Anthropic introduced a model tier "larger and more intelligent than our Opus models" (from a leaked draft that Anthropic confirmed), with capabilities "substantially beyond" any model it had trained. Its internal capability trend line bent upward. The model was released only to Project Glasswing partners.
